hints.title: Use medians to order the triples
hints.body: Write the sorted triples as (a, 8, b) and (c, 9, d). Their totals are 30 and 36, so a+b=22 and c+d=27.
hints.recap: Means give totals; medians give the middle entries.
hints.pitfall: All six entries are distinct, including entries in different triples.
hints.pause: What are the largest allowed integer values of a and c?

recall.reminder: For a sorted triple, the outer entries sum to three times its mean minus its median.

hints.title: Use distinctness across both triples
hints.body: We have a≤7. Also c<9 but c cannot equal 8, because 8 is already used; hence c≤7. If c=7, a cannot equal 7.
hints.recap: The lower entries compete for the same available integers.
hints.pitfall: Optimising each triple separately can choose the same entry twice.

recall.reminder: Distinctness applies to every entry of a construction, even across separate triples.

hints.title: Bound the range in each case
hints.body: Use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></math> in each of the cases from the previous hint. Bound the overall maximum from below and the overall minimum from above.
hints.recap: The range is the maximum minus the minimum across all six entries.
hints.pitfall: A construction alone does not rule out a smaller range.
hints.pause: Compute the two case bounds and build a pair of triples attaining the better one.

recall.reminder: The range is the maximum minus the minimum across all six entries.

solution:
Sort the triples as (a, 8, b) and (c, 9, d). Their means give a+b=22 and c+d=27. Since all six integers are distinct, a≤7 and c≤7: c cannot be 8 because 8 is already the first median.

If c=7, then d=20. Distinctness forces a≤6, so the overall range is at least 20−6=14.

If c≤6, then d=27−c≥21. The overall minimum is at most c≤6 and the maximum is at least d≥21, giving range at least 15. Thus no allowed choice has range below 14.

The triples (6, 8, 16) and (7, 9, 20) have means 10 and 12, medians 8 and 9, and six distinct integer entries. Their combined range is 20−6=14, attaining the bound.

Answer E: 14.
knowledgePattern: Optimise range subject to distinct integer means and medians
